setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 revenue was $9.45B, up 5.8% year on year and 5% sequentially. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.49, against $0.50 a year earlier. The GAAP figure includes a $187M non-cash pension settlement charge and $55M of ChampionX merger and integration cost.

Management's headline Q3 EPS excluding charges and credits was $0.64. That is up $0.09 sequentially and down $0.05 year on year. Company-wide adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.9%, up 71bp sequentially. Pretax margins rose in all four divisions. MarketBeat records the $0.64 as a beat against a $0.62 consensus, and revenue of $9.45B against $9.27B.

Q4 guide: revenue of about $10B (+5% to +7% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA margin up 100–150bp. It assumes Middle East revenue stays flat at about $1.9B, roughly 83% of Q4 2025. Core divisions are guided up low single digits, with Production Systems up high single digits and Well Construction and Reservoir Performance about flat. Digital is guided to its usual year-end uptick, led by exploration data.

Consensus for fiscal Q4 2026 is $10.01B revenue and $0.75 EPS, with the report expected 2027-01-21 after the close. Revenue consensus sits at the midpoint of the guided range, so a revenue beat needs the Middle East or year-end sales to surprise. The +36% EPS growth implied against Q4 2025 GAAP $0.55 is not like-for-like, because Q4 2025 carried $561M of pretax charges.

Reconciling the guide to EPS (my estimate): Q4 ex-charges pretax of about $1.47–1.55B, a roughly 20% tax rate, about $50M of NCI and about 1,485–1,490M diluted shares give adjusted EPS of about $0.75–0.80. Consensus $0.75 therefore sits at the low end of the guide-implied range, i.e. it embeds a small haircut to the margin guide. The 23% Q3 effective rate was inflated by the non-deductible pension charge and should not recur.

The Middle East is the swing factor. Nine-month Middle East revenue fell 16% (about $1.1B) on conflict-related operational disruption. Q3 Middle East revenue grew 13% sequentially to about $1.9B despite late-quarter disruptions. Management said the near-term recovery pace is uncertain and that resolution could unlock deferred activity.

Cash and leverage: nine-month free cash flow (company definition) was $1,521M against $1,826M a year earlier. Q3 FCF was $828M. Net debt was $9.25B against $7.42B at year-end. Receivables rose to $9.7B and inventories to $5.5B. Management expects a 'meaningful step-up' in Q4 FCF, with the size dependent on collection timing in certain countries.

Strategic overlay: SLB signed (Aug 31) to buy Kelvion for about $3.4B cash plus about $0.7B assumed debt, with closing expected in 1H27. Management targets Data Center Solutions above a $1B run rate by end-2026 and above $2B in 2027. The CFO says that business is not accretive to SLB's margin.
The average closing move over the last 8 reports is ±4.1%. No options-implied move is available yet, and no beat/miss record or sell-side revision trend could be sourced.

since_filing.text: Oil is high and headline-driven. Brent rose 1.3% and WTI 3% on Oct 28 on concerns over intensified Houthi attacks and other escalation. On Oct 29 they fell on hopes that peace talks may resume, with Brent about $114 and WTI about $101. No agreement or schedule was reported, and the full list of escalation drivers was not retrievable.

Forecasters raised oil views. UBS lifted its year-end Brent forecast to $110 from $100 on Oct 28, citing persistent Middle East supply disruption. A Reuters survey of 32 analysts put the 2026 Brent average at $92.88, above $90 for the first time since May. High prices reflect supply disruption rather than a confirmed activity upcycle.

Peer read-across on the Middle East is mixed. Reuters reports HAL's Middle East & Asia revenue rose 8% sequentially on Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. It reports that Baker Hughes expects Middle East activity to fall sequentially in Q4 on logistics costs and supply-chain challenges, and notes BKR has nearly 40% of revenue in the region. This is a risk to SLB's flat-Q4 assumption.

HAL's 10-Q (filed Oct 23) shows Q3 revenue of $5.7B. International led: Latin America +13% and Europe/Africa/CIS +23%. Middle East/Asia was flat year on year and North America fell 9% to $2.16B. HAL says North America customer activity is focused on maximizing returns within existing capital budgets. That points to soft North America activity at HAL, against the 7% sequential North America growth an analyst cited on SLB's call. SLB management ties its North America growth to ChampionX, drilling technology, digital and data centers.

Baker Hughes (Oct 28 call) expects global upstream spending broadly flat in 2026 with an improving outlook into 2027. That is more cautious than SLB's mid-single-digit 2027 OFS market growth, though both point to improvement. TPH Research is cited by Reuters as expecting about 9% annual SLB revenue growth excluding Kelvion, with Middle East recovery beginning in H2 2027. The period for the 9% is not stated explicitly.

Data-center thermal demand read-through: Trane announced the Cancoil acquisition on Oct 28 (price undisclosed, close expected by end-2026), and Vertiv's 10-Q shows Q3 net sales +61.2% on 'very robust' AI data-center demand. This supports the thermal-management thesis behind Kelvion but gives no valuation benchmark.

Reuters (Oct 28) notes SLB flagged renewed Middle East disruptions in the final weeks of Q3. This is consistent with the 10-Q 'late-quarter disruptions' and the call's 'heightened tensions' over recent weeks. Nothing in the retrieved post-filing material contradicts the filing or call figures. No direct evidence on Q4-to-date Middle East activity was found.

key_debates.question: Will Middle East revenue hold at about $1.9B in Q4?

bull.text: Q3 Middle East revenue rose 13% despite late-quarter disruptions. Four Aramco integrated well construction contracts (450+ wells over an initial three years) mobilize in Q4. HAL's Middle East & Asia revenue rose 8% sequentially, and peace-talk hopes could unlock deferred activity.

bear.text: Management described 'heightened tensions' and Houthi escalation is reported. Iraq lacked an uplift. BKR expects Middle East activity to fall sequentially in Q4, and HAL says recovery pace and breadth remain uncertain.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Middle East revenue against about $1.9B, commentary on Q4-to-date activity by country, and any peace-talk progress before the Jan 21 report.

key_debates.question: Is the +100–150bp Q4 margin step, and a 2027 margin expansion, credible?

bull.text: Operating leverage is strong because SLB kept Middle East resources in place. ChampionX EBITDA margins are in the mid-20s and rising, and synergies are ahead of plan. Digital margin should exceed 35% for the full year, and inflation and pricing pressure are 'baked in'.

bear.text: Well Construction margin fell 346bp over nine months, partly on pricing headwinds in select markets. Data Center Solutions is growing quickly but is not accretive to margin, with ramp-up costs already hitting All Other. HAL cites persistent inflation in logistics, chemicals and cement.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 division margins (Well Construction and Reservoir Performance versus Production Systems and Digital) and the January 2027 margin framework.

key_debates.question: Does the 2027 'mid-single-digit market growth with core outperformance' view hold up?

bull.text: Management cites third-party deepwater FIDs expected up more than 30% in 2026, renewed exploration, Venezuela revenue more than doubling in 2026, and OneSubsea bookings above $9B. TPH is cited as expecting about 9% growth, and oil is near $114.

bear.text: BKR sees upstream spending broadly flat in 2026 with only an 'improving' 2027. HAL's North America revenue fell 9%, and Venezuela is contested by HAL and BKR. A peace deal could pull crude back toward the $65–70 range raised on the call.

key_debates.what_settles_it: January 2027 guidance and customer budget commentary, OneSubsea order flow, and the oil price path.

key_debates.question: Is the Kelvion and Data Center Solutions pivot value-creating given leverage?

bull.text: Data Center Solutions is on track to surpass a $1B run rate by year-end and to surpass a $2B run rate in 2027. Peer Vertiv reports very robust demand growth for AI data centers. Management says customers like the combination with Kelvion, and the deal raises SLB's share of wallet per gigawatt.

bear.text: Kelvion costs about $4.1B including assumed debt, on top of $9.25B of net debt. By my estimate pro forma leverage would be about 1.5–1.6x before Kelvion EBITDA, which is undisclosed. Data Center Solutions dilutes margin. Funding mix and regulatory timing are not disclosed.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Kelvion financing and EBITDA disclosure, regulatory clearances, and Data Center Solutions margin and backlog disclosure.

key_debates.question: Is free cash flow enough to fund the $4B+ capital return plus Kelvion?

bull.text: Q4 is seasonally the strongest cash quarter. Q4 2025 FCF was about $2.29B, and receivables at about 95 days of revenue leave room for a collections release.

bear.text: Nine-month FCF fell to $1.52B, working capital absorbed $1.5B, and net debt is up $1.8B year to date. Full-year FCF of about $3.3–3.8B (my estimate) is below the roughly $4.15B of buybacks plus dividends, before the $3.4B Kelvion cash outlay.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 FCF and year-end net debt, and any change in 2027 buyback pacing.

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Revenue lands near the $10B guide ($9.9–10.1B, i.e. +5–7% on Q3's $9.45B) with the Middle East about flat at $1.9B. Production Systems rises high single digits on year-end product sales and Digital delivers a seasonal exploration uptick. Adjusted EBITDA margin reaches about 22.9–23.4% (21.9% plus the guided 100–150bp). Adjusted EPS is about $0.75–0.80, in line to slightly above the $0.75 consensus. Free cash flow steps up meaningfully from Q3's $828M, as management indicated. January 2027 guidance repeats mid-single-digit market growth.

triggers: Digital Q4 revenue near $900M or above

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Peace talks revive and Middle East activity rebounds above $1.9B. Year-end exploration data and product sales are strong, so revenue is above the top of the roughly $9.92–10.11B guided range and EBITDA margin is at or above 23.4% (the top of the guided 100–150bp expansion on 21.9%). Adjusted EPS is at or above $0.80. Free cash flow steps up well beyond Q3's $828M and net debt falls from the $9.25B at Q3. Management says a Middle East resolution would be a catalyst for additional 2027 growth on top of its mid-single-digit market outlook.

triggers: Credible resumption of regional peace talks

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Escalation (Houthi attacks, Hormuz disruption) or logistics constraints push Middle East revenue below $1.9B, as BKR expects for its own Q4. Year-end sales slip into 2027, Data Center Solutions ramp costs and amortization weigh on margins, and Q4 revenue falls below the $9.92B low end. EPS misses the $0.75 consensus, FCF disappoints on collections timing, and net debt stays near $8.6–8.9B with Kelvion looming. 2027 margin commentary is cautious.

triggers: Escalation affecting UAE, Kuwait or Saudi operations
Delayed year-end product or digital sales

claim.text: Middle East escalation or prolonged disruption could push activity below the flat-$1.9B guide assumption. Nine-month revenue in the region fell 16%, late-quarter disruptions occurred in Q3, and the guide explicitly excludes worst-case escalation.

Year-end timing risk. The Q4 step-up depends on year-end product sales and digital exploration licensing, and on collections timing in certain countries for free cash flow. Management did not quantify either.

Margin dilution and pricing. Data Center Solutions is not accretive to margin and carries ramp-up costs. Well Construction faced pricing headwinds in select markets. HAL cites persistent inflation in logistics, chemicals and cement.

An oil-price reversal on a Middle East settlement could weaken the longer-cycle investment narrative. Brent is about $114, and an analyst on the call raised the case of crude moderating to $65–70, as in June.

Earnings-quality and basis risk. GAAP EPS ($0.49 in Q3) differs materially from the ex-charges headline ($0.64). The basis of the $0.75 consensus is unconfirmed, and charges (pension, merger and integration, workforce) have recurred in every period shown.

questions_for_management.question: What is Middle East activity so far in Q4 by country (UAE, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Iraq), and what would a Houthi- or Hormuz-related escalation do to the $1.9B assumption? When do the Aramco integrated contracts reach full capacity?

why.text: The Q4 guide assumes flat Middle East revenue at about $1.9B, BKR guides the region down sequentially, and the SLB CEO said late-quarter activity adjustments were made.

questions_for_management.question: Bridge the Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin step of +100–150bp. How much comes from Digital Exploration, Middle East operating leverage and Production Systems, and how much does Data Center Solutions and higher exploration-data amortization offset? What tax rate, NCI and charges should we model?

why.text: The guide implies about $2.3B of EBITDA, roughly flat on Q4 2025's derived level, and consensus EPS of $0.75 sits at the low end of the guide-implied range.

questions_for_management.question: What gives you confidence that Well Construction and Reservoir Performance margins recover in 2027? Is the pricing pressure in select markets stabilizing, and where?

why.text: Well Construction margin contracted 346bp over nine months on Middle East disruption plus pricing headwinds, and the CFO hopes pricing pressure abates.

questions_for_management.question: How will Kelvion be financed (cash, debt, slower buybacks)? What are Kelvion's EBITDA and data-center revenue mix, which regulatory approvals are required, and does 2027 repurchase pacing change?

why.text: Kelvion adds about $4.1B of cash plus assumed debt against $9.25B of net debt. Remaining buyback authorization is about $2.37B before Q4 repurchases.

questions_for_management.question: What is the expected size of the Q4 free cash flow step-up, which countries drive collection timing, and why are receivables at about 95 days of revenue against about 82 at year-end?

why.text: Receivables rose to $9.7B, nine-month working capital absorbed $1.5B, and Q4 FCF must help cover about $4B of shareholder returns.

questions_for_management.question: What are Data Center Solutions' standalone margins and backlog, and what does the $2B 2027 run rate need in customer count and capacity? How large is Venezuela in 2027, and how do you hold share against HAL and BKR there?

why.text: The $2B 2027 run-rate target is roughly 2.1x Q3's implied Data Center Solutions run rate of about $0.94B (my arithmetic: Q3 revenue of about $235M, back-solved from the +$44M / +23% sequential increase). Management also says the business is not accretive to SLB's overall margin. HAL has re-established operations in Venezuela and BKR has signed two strategic agreements there.
